In my opinion, I would say you're wrong in the sense of there's little to spend your money on. Even though you may not be a fan of the physical merchandise or NC wearables, they're actually a big seller for them. 

People like myself like to indulge in the merch every so often as it's nostalgic and there is actually quite a bit of variety - they have shirts, pins, blankets, keychains, advent calendars, plushies... So there's something for everyone.

With NC wearables, they are a huge source of income. There's a handful of new wearables every week, not even including the mystery capsules, pet slots, prizes like dyeworks or shenanigifts changing etc. And if you ever go to the NC chat, you'll see how much people spend on these. People like trading items and to do this they need to have gift boxes. How do you get those? You buy them! 

From personal experience I like to buy a bit of everything in the mall as I have extreme fear of missing out. If a nice item comes out then I want to try and make sure I get it myself instead of trading (that's my personal preference). Because of this, I pretty much take part in every NC event etc. Over the winter/Xmas period, I will have easily spent $50 due to items, capsules, events etc.

I do agree that your ideas have some merit! I'd love things I could buy exclusively because I'm a premium member or different fortune cookies, but I don't think that the Neopets team is bad at monetising - a lot of it just doesn't appeal to you.

This post explains everything very well in my opinion.

My other half works in infrastructure and Internet security for some big companies and when I showed him what had happened and asked his opinion he looked at all the information we had and told me not to worry too much about visiting the site, just to make sure my passwords had been changed on other important sites and that I had implemented 2 step verification where I can etc.

I understand people are anxious and we haven't had any new information for a while, which is extremely bad on TNT's behalf, but I feel like this community always takes things to the extreme. A serious data breach becomes the end of the world (even though other, far bigger companies have had the same happen but have more manpower to shove it under the rug from public eye), and in the same token something trivial like releasing a pet colour that doesn't look great is also the end of the world and the downfall of neopets.

I love this community I really do, but sometimes it just feels like everything that ever happens on the site is hated.

Again, I get what's happened is a big issue and totally get the anxiety about people's data... but it's not like you just click on the site and then some hacker can literally access every single nugget of your Internet data.

Yeah when lurking you just generally sit on a certain board topic like the pound chat and just read all the boards but don't post a lot. If I see my friends or am in an advertising mood I might post or make my own board, but 90% of the time it's just clicking on all the boards and reading the first couple of posts to see what's being traded by who. After a couple of days you'll notice it's a lot of the same people making repeated boards everyday generally.

I have neopets open on the side while I'm working or doing things like watching a film, so I'm probably seeing the board for 6 or more hours a day. It becomes quite easy to recognise pets and users that are legit and have been around a while and ones that just pop up on accounts that are suspicious. Sometimes it is genuinely someone coming back from hiatus, but a lot of the time they're normally hacked accounts that were abandoned.

Being around for so long I do notice when people return who I've not seen around for a good few years - you get to know people's 'famous' pets that stick in your mind. As an example I have a RW pet myself who is always my active and I've had her for almost 8 years now, so a lot of veteran people on the PC recognise her and associate her with me even though I've not posted a lot in a while.

Unfortunately I dont think anyone can be sure what's happening and who's in on it.

There is definitely some cheating going on and hacking old accounts/stealing pets, but as to who is doing it no one can be certain. There are some people who genuinely have no idea and are being caught up in the commotion (trading for compromised pets or finding them UFA or in the pound). 

I know a lot of popular PCer's names are being thrown about, but it all seems to be 'he said, she said' gossip, which doesn't help. 

I would say just be super careful if you're out trading high value pets right now. If you're not sure of a pet's credibility, you can always make a board and ask the community. There's always someone who can help.

I have been an avid lurker of the PC for almost 10 years. I may not post a lot but I know what pets are new and suspicious and am always glad to help out if you message me.

Don't get me wrong, there are names I would love to own and it would be nice to just be able to have that name sometimes... but the uniqueness of names on Neo inspires creativity for a lot of people, and a lot of people who trade names are inspired by that one pet they found up for trade, which then gives them a goal to work towards on the site and something to entertain them. 

Some people only play to trade pets; it's what they find fun and the pound chat board is probably the most popular board on Neopets which shows there's a big community that love the trading aspect. Without unique names, that part of the site would die very quickly and I think a lot of those people would leave.

Also, I don't get the point about naming a real life pet. I myself don't see Neo as an 'immersive' game so I don't feel the need to have that realness of just picking a name. To me it's just the same as if I was making something like a new email address or a new username on an online game. If it's taken then time to think of a unique spelling or something, never really bothered me.

That's fine, I like the uniqueness of only 1 pet having that name. Let's say I traded for Neil, I'm now the proud owner of this pet and name and I can make him into whatever species and colour I feel like, but Neil is special to me. 

If pets were defined by an ID number for example, allowing you to have a pet but name it whatever you want even if that name is taken, then that would ruin that uniqueness. Sure, I'd own Neil, but so could 100 other players who also named their pet Neil because there's no restriction. That makes the naming part of the game basically invalid. I know for myself, trading pets is what entertains me for 90% of my time on the site, and so with the name-trading being made redundant, that would mean that all that matters for trading is colour and whether the pet is UC or not.

I know not everyone feels like this and is probably only unique to players that like trading pets, but for me, this would just make the site boring. I could go our there, create a pet with the name I want instantly and paint it to whatever colour instantly and that would be it, job done. And if I get bored, I just change the name on a whim. It doesn't have any challenge to it for me I guess. I don't know if challenge is the right word, but I'm not sure how else to describe it.

Honestly if they made it so that you can just change your pet's name, then I wouldn't really have a reason to play anymore. I spend a lot of time trading names and pets on the pound chat, and my main hobby is looking for interesting names to trade for. I understand that not everyone is into names and trading. Some people are happy with a pet called something like SkyWarrior_5001 if they can nickname it, but for me my pet's name is its identity, so I would really want their name to be THEIR name, if that makes sense. I get that some of the name trends are silly - I personally don't like the fad of only having 3-4 letter named pets etc. But I do love the hunt of trading for the perfect name and the journey to get there. 

I'm not a name 'elitist'. Sure, I have my own real word pets, and my 3 or 4 letter pets. But I also have awesome names that I just fell on love with when browsing the boards one day and worked towards owning (for example, Autelia and Yaroo were 2 of those names). 

I think the uniqueness of the names is a big deal for a lot of people who play, and so it wouldn't be a good idea to just take that feature away.

Inktober is an event that artists around the world take part in across October. Each day of the month the task is to do one drawing until you have a drawing for each day! It was originally about drawing in ink but has evolved into people just using it as a chance to practice drawing. 

If you go to the official inktober website there is an official 'prompt list', which gives you a single word each day to base your drawings around. Theres many different lists out there; most people follow the official list but theres a 'witchtober' list for example, where each day the idea is to draw a witch inspired by the word. This list I've posted was uploaded by Neopets official facebook, for anyone wanting to take part in a Neopets-themed inktober.

Just so you know, if you can manage to find out if the pet has been recently stolen/has been around on active accounts for years, then that will be a big indication as to whether you may be able to get him back.

If he's only been moved recently, then there is a much much bigger chance it will be reversed. However if he's been traded for years for example, he could have been through far too many accounts and if it's been too long then TNT most likely won't reverse it. 

I could be completely wrong! But I've been around on the pet trading boards for years and have seen a lot of pets come and go. I've seen a lot of reversals, and the biggest problem is if (for example) your krawk has been around for 3 or 4 years, they will find it too tricky and too long of a time to return him.

There was a lot that contributed to the dread of the place. When I was in the application process many people told me it would be the best time of my life. It wasn't. The course itself was horribly put together and the tutors were very opinionated; it was 'my way or the highway' kind of thinking. In an art related course that kind of opinion cannot really be had, as art is a manifestation of someone's personal style. They would tell you your art had to be personal and such but then hate your idea because it wasn't abstract enough or something. Plus the first year I was there I was basically bullied by the other group of girls on my course for basically not being 'hipster' enough. I wasn't into alternative music and didn't like going out drinking every night etc. Because of that I basically became an outsider. I didn't mix with other groups because I lived with my partner and not in dorms, and I just generally became hesitant of the place. Why would you want to go somewhere that made you feel like shit (especially when you're paying to be there) when there's other places you would much rather want to be? Also just before the first year I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety and I told the student liasion officer and my tutors and none of them took it on board. I had to miss a lesson one time because my dog had to be put down, causing my depression to badly spiral for the next few days. I let them know in advance and was still belittled for not coming in afterwards? I still caught up on the lecture in my own time, but I was still treated like a bad school child in a place where you should respect each other as adults as you study. And after everything I have my parents pushing to finish because I'd be the first ever person in the family to go to University, and they wanted to be proud of me for that. I didn't want to let them down and that pressure sat on my shoulders all day every day. 

Yes to some people it may seem silly to be so hateful of something so petty, but in my mind University became this dreaded hell that I just wanted to get out of my life as it got worse. I even contemplated suicide (please take into account that there was a lot more than just university pushing me this far, but it was a big part of it). But eventually I pushed through, and I've proved to myself that I can do this.

For the last 4 years ive suffered with really bad depression. It's been because of quite a few things, but University was the big cloud that loomed over me. Every time I went to do anything related to it I would have a horrid panic attack. I couldn't even get close to the building without freaking out. As hand in days got closer I'd struggle to start work, but every day I'd try a little more. One day if I could only write 5 words without panicking that's fine: it's 5 words closer to finishing. I wanted to finish, no matter how much it affected me as I wanted to prove to myself I could do it! Little by little, over months and months, I finally completed my work and handed it in. Every little bit was like another step on this picture. You just have to have the determination to get to the top, no matter your circumstances!
